A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SPIRE and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting reliable comparison. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations on SIRST-UAVB and SIRST4, PRPS and HRPE ablations, and qualitative detection results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds matching-threshold evaluations and measured inference-speed comparisons.

M1.justification: PRPS construction, HRPE architecture, regression training objective, and peak-based inference are retained. Renaming gradient-aware modulation as contrast-aware modulation and expanding the NMS and candidate-selection description do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions use SIRST-UAVB and SIRST4, with the same constituent datasets, scene coverage, and centroid-localization task. The added matching-threshold tests change evaluation tolerance, not the represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine quantitative baselines, and Figure 4 retains its qualitative comparators, including P2P-HDNet. The new threshold and speed comparisons reuse DNANet, SCTransNet, and SDSNet; no comparison method is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported initial learning rate from 0.01 to 0.005 and SPIRE training from 400 to 500 epochs. v2 also adds matching tolerances of 3, 8, and 10 pixels alongside the retained default of 5, plus FPS evaluation. Splits and input resolutions remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 2 and Section 4.3 test sensitivity to centroid-matching tolerance on SIRST4. Section 3.4 additionally reports qualitative stability findings for confidence threshold and candidate-count settings, without detailed sweeps. Existing supervision, scale, stride, and component ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added evaluations do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark and retained ablation values are unchanged. New Table 2 reports SPIRE at the newly tested δ=3 with recall 92.93%, F1 94.74%, and Fa 18.61×10^-8, and identical results across δ=5,8,10. It adds FPS values of 261.2 for SPIRE, 80.86 for DNANet, 67.09 for SCTransNet, and 46.97 for SDSNet.

T1.justification: The PRPS, encoder, coordinate-refinement, and metric mathematics remain equivalent. Section 3.4 introduces intermediate notation for the suppressed heatmap and thresholded peak set, restating the existing local-maximum and top-N selection rule. No substantive derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof changes.

C1.justification: v1's contribution statement says post-processing pipelines become unnecessary; v2 explicitly acknowledges deterministic peak extraction as lightweight post-processing. The abstract and conclusion adopt this narrower description while retaining the central centroid-regression, single-point-supervision, and encoder-only contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added threshold results as supporting δ=5, relating stricter matching to the average target radius of 3.31 pixels. It also adds a qualification that overlapping response supports need not merge targets when separable maxima remain, and interprets FPS measurements as evidence of practical throughput benefits.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 newly specifies that Nmax equals each dataset's maximum target count and explains response-ranked candidate selection. Training hyperparameters are revised, and the existing repository link is now advertised for both code and benchmark. Numerical confidence-threshold settings and detailed timing procedures remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 42 works and retain the same positioning against segmentation, point-supervised methods, and heatmap approaches. Reference changes correct authors, publication details, and redundant metadata, with corresponding citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 polishes the abstract and introduction, revises modulation terminology, expands inference explanations, and renames Sections 3.4 and 4.3. It updates author order and correspondence information and adds acknowledgements. The main narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the threshold/FPS table, relocates Table 1, and renumbers the retained ablation tables. Figures 1 and 3 receive label revisions; Figures 4 and 5 receive styling and annotation adjustments. Existing figures and cases remain, with limited page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim precision, discloses Nmax, and adds direct speed measurements. However, its new robustness evidence needs clarification: Table 2 lowers both SPIRE recall and Fa when δ decreases from 5 to 3, which is inconsistent with changing only matching tolerance on fixed predictions under Section 4.1. The revised training settings also accompany unchanged retained scores without explanation. These unresolved issues prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
